brief.headline: Offer faster payment in exchange for a price discount — they're loss-making (net margin -199.2%) and highly leveraged (220.44x D/E), so they need cash, but a deep price cut risks our supply continuity.

priceAsk.summary: Request a price reduction tied to faster payment or committed volume, not a standalone cut
priceAsk.target: No best-price benchmark available; anchor any discount discussion to HDPE resin import unit value of 87.61 ₹/kg and position our ask as cost-pass-through fairness
priceAsk.basis: They earn far below peers (net margin -199.2% vs peer median 2.3%) and are loss-making (PAT ₹-22.50 Cr), so a headline price cut alone threatens continuity — instead, trade faster cash for a modest discount

paymentTermAsk.summary: Maintain current 30 Days After Receipt terms, or offer 15-day acceleration in exchange for a price concession
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Moving to 15 days earlier would free ₹2.60 L working capital for us, but costs them cash they don't have — use it as a trade, not a demand

brief.financialLeverage: Bprex is in severe distress: net margin -199.2% vs peer median 2.3%, EBITDA margin -87.3%, return on capital -10.2%, and debt-to-equity 220.44x with interest coverage -3.71x. They posted a ₹-22.50 Cr loss in FY2023-24 and carry a Probe42 score of 1/10 with health grade D (0/100). Our ₹63.21 L spend is 5.60% of their ₹11.29 Cr revenue — meaningful enough to command attention, but not so large we can bully them into a price cut that kills supply. Their cash-conversion cycle is 335d vs peer median 70d, so they value speed; they stretch payables to 226d vs peer 41d, so asking for longer credit is tone-deaf. Push gently: offer cash or volume certainty for a discount, and keep alternates warm.

evidence.point: They are loss-making and far below peer profitability
evidence.figure: Net margin -199.2% vs peer median 2.3%; PAT ₹-22.50 Cr in FY2023-24

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter with pharma bottles, caps, and preforms capability — top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader with strong pharma fit (pails, containers, bottles/closures) and health grade A — robust alternate

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging supplier with broad bottle/cap capability

risks: Their loss-making status (net margin -199.2%, PAT ₹-22.50 Cr) and 1/10 Probe42 score mean aggressive price pressure could trigger supply failure — don't over-push
High leverage (220.44x D/E) and negative interest coverage (-3.71x) flag potential solvency issues — qualify alternates now, don't wait
Asking for extended payment terms is a non-starter: they already stretch payables to 226d vs peer 41d and run a 335d cash cycle — they need cash in, not out
We're only 5.60% of their revenue, so while meaningful, we lack the scale to dictate terms unilaterally — frame asks as partnership, not ultimatum
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership and want to grow volume with you, but given the tight market and our own cost pressures, we'd like to explore a modest price adjustment in exchange for faster payment or a volume commitment — what works for you?
